evidence.quote: we implement online stability stopping for LangFlow and static schedule truncation for ELF, reducing denoiser evaluations by 12–25% while achieving 0.86–
0.94 paired-token agreement, with measurable quality trade-offs. The analysis further examines the dynamics of self-distilled ELF weights,

The analysis further examines the dynamics of self-distilled ELF weights, noting observable shifts in their commit clock and feature activation profile.
(iii) Online stopping and static schedule truncation informed by trajectory measurements, with evaluation savings assessed alongside output agreement and generation quality.

Continuous flow language models (CFLMs) represent a recent alternative to autoregressive (AR) Language Models and discrete Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) for generative language modeling.
embedding-space models such as LangFlow (Chen et al., 2026) and ELF (Hu et al., 2026). We study the latter, which refine continuous text embeddings from Gaussian noise.
Continuous Flow Language Models (CFLMs) generate text by integrating a learned velocity field from noise to the sequences of embeddings that represent texts,
LangFlow and ELF operate in embedding space and expose a prediction ˆxt of the clean terminal state conditioned on the current interpolant xt.
Self-conditioning guidance combines predictions and velocities with the same affine weights, preserving this identity in exact arithmetic for the unconditional protocol.
In this process, all token states are refined concurrently within a continuous space.
CFLMs update all positions simultaneously over T steps, with bidirectional interaction and state refinement until the last step.
They do not name exclusive concepts. ELF edits enter the next self-conditioning prediction after the current state update, rather than directly modifying that update.
